narrow_claim: Across multiple tested LLM families and knowledge domains, exposure to a unanimous incorrect majority can increase the probability that a model changes or selects an answer toward that majority; lower initial confidence increases susceptibility.

findings: all tested models showed varying conformity toward majority answers
higher initial confidence predicted greater resistance
instruction-tuned models were more resistant than base counterparts
more natural/conversational majority tone amplified conformity
Devil's Advocate and Question Distillation reduced conformity

verified_primary_lines.paper: Can LLM Agents Really Debate? A Controlled Study of Multi-Agent Debate in Logical Reasoning
verified_primary_lines.finding: Majority pressure can suppress independent correction; group diversity and intrinsic reasoning strength are dominant success factors.
Consensus interaction can propagate errors because correct agents may be influenced by incorrect agents; majority voting can degrade performance in some settings.

verified_primary_lines.paper: Minority Sentinel: When to Overturn Majority Voting in Multi-Agent LLM Debates
verified_primary_lines.finding: Correlated LLM errors violate naive independence assumptions behind majority voting; a correct minority can be systematically suppressed.

related_but_distinct_effects.relation: single-user preference or belief pressure rather than peer-majority pressure

independence_summary.warning: The 2026 multi-agent papers study debate architectures rather than exact replications of the 2025 Asch-style protocol; they strengthen the broader majority-pressure/error-propagation claim, not every narrow parameter estimate.

score_note: This is a corpus-maturity score for the narrow operational claim, not a probability that every model will conform in every setting.
r2_rule: Count independent evidence-producing lineages, not answer multiplicity. Correlated agents, cloned prompts, shared checkpoints or shared retrieval sources must be down-weighted before majority aggregation.
